title: A new feature edge can create a feature cycle — break it with a caller-injected port or lazy import, not a deep import
trigger: check-feature-cycles or check-deep-imports fails after wiring a new feature into existing ones
principle: Cross-feature imports may only go through the feature's index.ts barrel, and the feature dependency graph must stay acyclic — test files count as edges too. When a needed service lives in the wrong feature (a sink service under a producer feature), move it to its true owner rather than import across. When the needed capability would re-create a cycle, inject it as a function parameter (port) from the composition layer that already depends on both features. When the dependency is heavy UI only needed on a rare action, dynamic import() keeps it out of the lean entrypoint bundle and out of jsdom test module graphs — but jest.mock the barrel, not deep paths, since guards scan imports in tests too.

cases.context: miningQueue.quickAddQueueItem imported addToOceanSrs from dictionaryPopup — created cycle dictionaryPopup→subtitle→miningQueue→dictionaryPopup; static cardCreator barrel import also crashed jsdom tests via unrelated UI exports
cases.bad: import { addToOceanSrs } from '@/features/dictionaryPopup'; import { quickAddNote } from '@/features/cardCreator' in queueActions.ts
cases.good: Move addToOceanSrs to features/srs (its true owner); type OceanSrsAdder port injected by mountUniversalPanel; anki path uses await import('@/features/cardCreator') so the dialog stack stays lazy and test-mockable at the barrel

applyFor: wiring a new feature that needs an existing feature's service
jest module-graph crashes from barrel side-effects
keeping heavy dialogs out of lean bundles
